source.text: וְעַתָּ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל שְׁמַ֤ע אֶל־הַֽחֻקִּים֙ וְאֶל־הַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָֽנֹכִ֛י מְלַמֵּ֥ד אֶתְכֶ֖ם לַעֲשׂ֑וֹת לְמַ֣עַן תִּֽחְי֗וּ וּבָאתֶם֙ וִֽירִשְׁתֶּ֣ם אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבֹתֵיכֶ֖ם נֹתֵ֥ן לָכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, Israel, listen to the statutes and to the judgments that I [am] teaching you to do, so that you may live and go in and take possession of the land that Yahweh, [the] God of your fathers, [is] giving to you.

en.L: And now, Israel, listen to the statutes and to the judgments that I [am] teaching you to do, so that you may live, and go in and take possession of the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [the] God of your fathers, [is] giving you.
en.B: Now, Israel, listen to the statutes and rulings that I am teaching you to put into practice. Then you will live, and you will enter and take possession of the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestors, is giving you.
en.R: Now, Israel, listen to the laws and rules I am teaching you, and obey them. Then you will live, and you will go in and take possession of the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestors, is giving you.

decisions.choice: And now: the turn from what has happened to what Israel must do
decisions.reason: Chapters 1-3 retell the journey from Horeb to the plains of Moab. "And now" draws the lesson from that history: the God who has led them this far calls them to listen and obey. The rest of chapter 4 is the close of Moses' first speech.

decisions.choice: statutes and judgments: the whole body of God's law
decisions.reason: The two words are often paired in Deuteronomy (4:5, 8, 14; 5:1; 12:1). The first is a fixed rule or decree; the second a ruling, a decision about what is right in a case. Together they name everything Moses is about to teach.

decisions.choice: so that you may live: life in the land comes with obedience
decisions.reason: To live is more than to survive. It is the full life God gives his people in the land, and Deuteronomy ties it again and again to listening to him (4:4, 40; 30:15-20). The verse sets life before them as the goal of the law.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "fathers" means the forebears of the people, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and those after them. Balanced and Readable say "ancestors"; Literal keeps "fathers".

decisions.choice: Then you will live
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable split the long sentence and make the result of obeying a sentence of its own.

source.text: לֹ֣א תֹסִ֗פוּ עַל־הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אָנֹכִי֙ מְצַוֶּ֣ה אֶתְכֶ֔ם וְלֹ֥א תִגְרְע֖וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ לִשְׁמֹ֗ר אֶת־מִצְוֺת֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י מְצַוֶּ֥ה אֶתְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Not you shall add to the word that I [am] commanding you, and not you shall take away from it, to keep [the] commandments of Yahweh your God that I [am] commanding you.

en.L: You shall not add to the word that I [am] commanding you, and you shall not take away from it, so as to keep the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God that I [am] commanding you.
en.B: Add nothing to the word I am commanding you, and take nothing away from it, so that you keep the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God that I am giving you.
en.R: Do not add anything to what I command you, and do not take anything away from it. Just obey the commands of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God that I am giving you.

decisions.choice: the word: all that Moses commands, taken as one whole
decisions.reason: "Word" is singular. It sums up the whole of what Moses is commanding as a single message from God, not one saying among many.

decisions.choice: neither add nor take away: the command stands as God gave it
decisions.reason: No one may improve God's law by adding rules of their own, or soften it by leaving parts out. Deuteronomy repeats the warning at 13:1 (Hebrew numbering), and Proverbs 30:6 and Revelation 22:18-19 echo it.

decisions.choice: to keep: the way to keep the commandments is to leave them unchanged
decisions.reason: The infinitive "to keep" shows the purpose of the two warnings: by neither adding nor removing, Israel keeps God's commandments as they are.

decisions.choice: I am giving you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "I am commanding you" twice. Balanced and Readable say "giving" the second time to avoid the repetition; Literal keeps both.

source.text: עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ הָֽרֹאֹ֔ת אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה בְּבַ֣עַל פְּע֑וֹר כִּ֣י כָל־הָאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הָלַךְ֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י בַֽעַל־פְּע֔וֹר הִשְׁמִיד֛וֹ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ מִקִּרְבֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Your eyes [are] the [ones] seeing what did Yahweh at Baal-peor; for every man who walked after Baal-peor, destroyed him Yahweh your God from your midst.

en.L: Your eyes [are] the ones that saw what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did at Baal-peor; for every man who walked after Baal-peor, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God destroyed him from your midst.
en.B: Your own eyes have seen what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did at Baal-peor: every man who went after the Baal of Peor, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God wiped out from among you.
en.R: You saw for yourselves what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did at Baal-peor. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God wiped out every man among you who worshiped the god Baal there.

decisions.choice: Baal-peor: Israel's worship of the god of Peor in Moab
decisions.reason: Numbers 25:1-9 tells how men of Israel joined the Moabites in worshiping Baal of Peor, and how those who did died in a plague. The people Moses now speaks to saw it happen only a short time before.

decisions.choice: walked after: followed as a god, gave loyalty and worship
decisions.reason: To walk after a god is to follow and serve it (6:14; 8:19). The picture is of a servant walking behind a master.

decisions.choice: Baal-peor: the name both of the place and of the god worshiped there
decisions.reason: "At Baal-peor" names the place; "after Baal-peor" names the god, "Baal" (lord, master) of Peor. The same name serves for both.

decisions.choice: every man: the men who joined in that worship
decisions.reason: The word can mean "each person", but Numbers 25 tells of men who joined themselves to Baal of Peor through Moabite women, and "every man" fits that account.

decisions.choice: who worshiped the god Baal there
decisions.reason: Readable explains "walked after Baal-peor" and says that Baal was a god.

source.text: וְאַתֶּם֙ הַדְּבֵקִ֔ים בַּיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם חַיִּ֥ים כֻּלְּכֶ֖ם הַיּֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: But you, the [ones] holding fast to Yahweh your God, [are] alive all of you this day.

en.L: But you who held fast to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God [are] alive, all of you, this day.
en.B: But you who clung to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God are alive today, every one of you.
en.R: But all of you who stayed loyal to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God are still alive today.

decisions.choice: holding fast: clinging, staying joined in loyalty
decisions.reason: The word means to stick or cling to something. It is used of a man joined to his wife (Genesis 2:24) and of Israel's loyalty to God (10:20; 13:5 in Hebrew numbering; 30:20).

decisions.choice: alive: the living, set against those who died at Peor
decisions.reason: Those who followed Baal died; those who held to the LORD live. The contrast shows what verse 1 means by "so that you may live".

decisions.choice: stayed loyal
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for the picture of clinging to God.

source.text: רְאֵ֣ה׀לִמַּ֣דְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֗ם חֻקִּים֙ וּמִשְׁפָּטִ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוַּ֖נִי יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑י לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת כֵּ֔ן בְּקֶ֣רֶב הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֛ם בָּאִ֥ים שָׁ֖מָּה לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: See, I have taught you statutes and judgments, just as commanded me Yahweh my God, to do so in [the] midst of the land where you [are] going there to take possession of it.

en.L: See, I have taught you statutes and judgments just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God commanded me, to do so in the midst of the land that you [are] going into to take possession of it.
en.B: See, I have taught you statutes and rulings, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God commanded me, for you to live by in the land you are going into to take possession of.
en.R: Listen: I have taught you laws and rules, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God told me to. You are to obey them in the land you are about to enter and take possession of.

decisions.choice: See: a call for attention
decisions.reason: "See" here does not ask anyone to look at something. It calls the hearers to take note of what follows.

decisions.choice: as the LORD my God commanded me: Moses teaches only what God gave him
decisions.reason: Moses claims no law of his own. What he teaches comes from God, who commanded him to teach it (verse 14; 1:3).

decisions.choice: in the midst of the land: the law is meant for life in the land
decisions.reason: The statutes are given now, before the crossing, to be done once Israel lives in the land. Much of the law assumes a settled people with towns, fields and courts.

decisions.choice: Listen
decisions.reason: Readable says "Listen" so that young readers do not take "See" as an order to look.

source.text: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם֮ וַעֲשִׂיתֶם֒ כִּ֣י הִ֤וא חָכְמַתְכֶם֙ וּבִ֣ינַתְכֶ֔ם לְעֵינֵ֖י הָעַמִּ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִשְׁמְע֗וּן אֵ֚ת כָּל־הַחֻקִּ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וְאָמְר֗וּ רַ֚ק עַם־חָכָ֣ם וְנָב֔וֹן הַגּ֥וֹי הַגָּד֖וֹל הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you shall keep and do [them], for it [is] your wisdom and your understanding in [the] eyes of the peoples who will hear all the statutes these, and they will say, surely a people wise and understanding [is] the nation great this.

en.L: And you shall keep and do [them], for that [is] your wisdom and your understanding in the eyes of the peoples, who will hear all these statutes and say, 'Surely this great nation [is] a wise and understanding people.'
en.B: Keep them and follow them, for that is what will make you wise and understanding in the eyes of the peoples. When they hear about all these statutes, they will say, 'This great nation is truly a wise and understanding people.'
en.R: Obey these laws carefully. That is how the other nations will see how wise and understanding you are. They will hear about all these laws and say, 'What a wise and understanding people this great nation is!'

decisions.choice: it: the keeping and doing of the statutes
decisions.reason: "It" points back to what Israel does: keeping and doing the law is what makes them wise in others' sight, not merely having it.

decisions.choice: wisdom and understanding: skill in living and insight into what is right
decisions.reason: In the Old Testament wisdom is practical: knowing how to live well before God and others (Proverbs 1:2-7). Understanding is the ability to see into things and judge rightly.

decisions.choice: surely: an exclamation of surprise and admiration
decisions.reason: The small word often means "only", but at the head of a saying like this it stresses what follows: "truly", "indeed".

decisions.choice: What a wise and understanding people this great nation is!
decisions.reason: Readable turns the nations' words into an exclamation, which carries the force of "surely" in plain English.

source.text: כִּ֚י מִי־ג֣וֹי גָּד֔וֹל אֲשֶׁר־ל֥וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים קְרֹבִ֣ים אֵלָ֑יו כַּיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ בְּכָּל־קָרְאֵ֖נוּאֵלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: For who [is] a nation great that has to it gods near to it like Yahweh our God in all our calling to him?

en.L: For what great nation [is there] that has gods [so] near to it as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God [is] whenever we call to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?
en.B: For what great nation has gods as near to it as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God is to us whenever we call to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?
en.R: No other nation, however great, has gods as near to it as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God is to us. He is near whenever we call out to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: gods near: the nations' gods, compared with Israel's God
decisions.reason: The word for God or gods is plural in form, and here its adjective "near" is plural too. That suggests "gods", the gods of other nations. But a plural adjective is used with Israel's God as well (Joshua 24:19), so the line may mean "a god so near". Either way the point is the same: no nation has a god who comes near as the LORD does.

decisions.choice: who? : a question that expects the answer "none"
decisions.reason: Moses asks the question to make a point. No great nation has such a god.

decisions.choice: call to him: pray, cry out for help
decisions.reason: To call to God is to pray to him, especially in need (Psalm 145:18). The LORD's nearness is shown in his hearing and answering.

decisions.choice: No other nation, however great, has ...
decisions.reason: Readable states the answer the question expects instead of asking it, and repeats "near" in a second sentence to keep the sentences short.

source.text: וּמִי֙ גּ֣וֹי גָּד֔וֹל אֲשֶׁר־ל֛וֹ חֻקִּ֥ים וּמִשְׁפָּטִ֖ים צַדִּיקִ֑ם כְּכֹל֙ הַתּוֹרָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָנֹכִ֛י נֹתֵ֥ן לִפְנֵיכֶ֖ם הַיּֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And who [is] a nation great that has to it statutes and judgments righteous like all the law this which I [am] setting before you today?

en.L: And what great nation [is there] that has statutes and judgments [as] righteous as all this law that I [am] setting before you today?
en.B: And what great nation has statutes and rulings as righteous as this whole law that I put before you today?
en.R: And no other nation, however great, has laws and rules as right and fair as all this teaching I am giving you today.

decisions.choice: righteous: right, fair, in line with what is just
decisions.reason: The word describes what matches the right standard: laws that are fair and good, which treat people justly. God himself is the standard (32:4).

decisions.choice: law: the whole of Moses' teaching
decisions.reason: As at 1:5, the word means instruction, everything Moses teaches about how Israel is to live with God, not only rules.

decisions.choice: right and fair ... teaching
decisions.reason: Readable says "right and fair" for the one Hebrew word and "teaching" for the law, as Deuteronomy's terms call for. It states the answer to the question, as in verse 7.

source.text: רַ֡ק הִשָּׁ֣מֶר לְךָ֩ וּשְׁמֹ֨ר נַפְשְׁךָ֜ מְאֹ֗ד פֶּן־תִּשְׁכַּ֨ח אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֜ים אֲשֶׁר־רָא֣וּ עֵינֶ֗יךָ וּפֶן־יָס֨וּרוּ֙ מִלְּבָ֣בְךָ֔ כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֣י חַיֶּ֑יךָ וְהוֹדַעְתָּ֥ם לְבָנֶ֖יךָ וְלִבְנֵ֥י בָנֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Only take care for yourself and guard your soul exceedingly, lest you forget the things that have seen your eyes, and lest they depart from your heart all [the] days of your life; and you shall make them known to your children and to [the] children of your children,

en.L: Only take care for yourself, and guard your soul greatly, lest you forget the things that your eyes have seen, and lest they depart from your heart all the days of your life; and you shall make them known to your {{gender:children|sons}} and to your {{gender:children's children|sons' sons}},
en.B: Only guard yourself and keep close watch over your life, so that you do not forget what your own eyes have seen, and so that it does not leave your mind for as long as you live. Make it known to your {{gender:children|sons}} and your {{gender:grandchildren|grandsons}},
en.R: But be careful, and keep watch over yourselves. Never forget the things you saw with your own eyes. Keep them in your minds as long as you live. Teach them to your {{gender:children|sons}} and {{gender:grandchildren|grandsons}}.

decisions.choice: your soul: yourself, your life
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word often called "soul" means the living person, the self. To guard one's soul is to watch over oneself.

decisions.choice: you (singular): the people addressed as one
decisions.reason: Moses moves between "you" plural and "you" singular. The singular speaks to Israel as one people, and to each person in it.

decisions.choice: heart: the mind and memory
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the heart is where a person thinks, remembers and decides. Things that depart from the heart are forgotten.

decisions.choice: make them known to your children: memory passed from one generation to the next
decisions.reason: What Israel saw is to be told to children and grandchildren who did not see it (6:7, 20-25; 11:19). Faith rests on remembered acts of God.

decisions.choice: grandchildren
decisions.reason: "Your children's children" is "grandchildren" in plain English. Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase.

decisions.choice: yourselves
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plural, since Moses is speaking to the whole people; Literal and Balanced keep the singular form.

source.text: י֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָמַ֜דְתָּ לִפְנֵ֨י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶיךָ֮ בְּחֹרֵב֒ בֶּאֱמֹ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י הַקְהֶל־לִי֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם וְאַשְׁמִעֵ֖ם אֶת־דְּבָרָ֑י אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִלְמְד֜וּן לְיִרְאָ֣ה אֹתִ֗י כָּל־הַיָּמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵ֤ם חַיִּים֙ עַל־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה וְאֶת־בְּנֵיהֶ֖ם יְלַמֵּדֽוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: [the] day that you stood before Yahweh your God at Horeb, when said Yahweh to me, assemble for me the people, and I will make them hear my words, that they may learn to fear me all the days that they [are] alive on the ground, and their children they may teach.

en.L: the day that you stood before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God at Horeb, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Assemble the people for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will make them hear {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words, so that they may learn to fear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} all the days that they [are] alive on the ground, and [that] they may teach their {{gender:children|sons}}.'
en.B: above all the day you stood before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God at Horeb, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Gather the people to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will let them hear {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words. Then they will learn to fear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as long as they live on the earth, and they will teach their {{gender:children|sons}} to do the same.'
en.R: Tell them about the day you stood in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God at Mount Horeb. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Bring the people together in front of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I will let them hear what I say. Then they will learn to honor and fear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as long as they live on the earth. And they will teach their {{gender:children|sons}} to do the same.'

decisions.choice: the day: the chief of the things Israel saw (verse 9)
decisions.reason: "The day" stands beside "the things" of verse 9 and names the greatest of them: the day at Horeb when God spoke.

decisions.choice: Horeb: the mountain called Sinai in Exodus
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy calls the mountain of the covenant Horeb (1:6; 5:2). Exodus 19 tells the same events at Mount Sinai.

decisions.choice: fear me: reverent awe that leads to obedience
decisions.reason: To fear God is to take him seriously, with awe and respect, and so to obey him (6:2, 13, 24; 10:12). It is a fear to be learned, not panic.

decisions.choice: above all
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "above all" so that the day at Horeb reads as the chief thing to be remembered and told, as the Hebrew means.

decisions.choice: Tell them about ... Mount Horeb
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence with "Tell them about", taking up "make them known" from verse 9, and says that Horeb is a mountain.

source.text: וַתִּקְרְב֥וּן וַתַּֽעַמְד֖וּן תַּ֣חַת הָהָ֑ר וְהָהָ֞ר בֹּעֵ֤ר בָּאֵשׁ֙ עַד־לֵ֣ב הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם חֹ֖שֶׁךְ עָנָ֥ן וַעֲרָפֶֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And you came near and stood under the mountain, and the mountain [was] burning with fire to [the] heart of the heavens: darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.

en.L: And you came near and stood under the mountain, and the mountain [was] burning with fire to the heart of the heavens: darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.
en.B: You drew near and stood at the base of the mountain. It was burning with fire up into the heart of the sky, wrapped in darkness, cloud, and deep gloom.
en.R: You came close and stood at the bottom of the mountain. Fire was blazing on the mountain, reaching high into the sky. All around it were darkness and cloud and thick blackness.

decisions.choice: to the heart of the heavens: high up into the sky
decisions.reason: The "heart" of something is its middle. The flames reached into the midst of the sky, as high as the eye could see.

decisions.choice: fire, cloud and thick darkness: the scene at Sinai
decisions.reason: Exodus 19:16-18 and 20:21 describe the same scene: smoke, fire, thunder and a thick cloud on the mountain where God came down. Moses repeats it in 5:22-23.

decisions.choice: darkness, cloud, and thick darkness: what surrounded the fire
decisions.reason: The three nouns stand loosely after the clause, describing the mountain: it burned with fire and was covered in darkness at the same time.

decisions.choice: at the base of / at the bottom of
decisions.reason: "Under the mountain" means at its foot. Balanced and Readable say so; Literal keeps "under".

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם מִתּ֣וֹךְ הָאֵ֑שׁ ק֤וֹל דְּבָרִים֙ אַתֶּ֣ם שֹׁמְעִ֔ים וּתְמוּנָ֛ה אֵינְכֶ֥ם רֹאִ֖ים זוּלָתִ֥י קֽוֹל׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to you from [the] midst of the fire; [the] sound of words you [were] hearing, but a form not you [were] seeing, only a voice.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to you from the midst of the fire. The sound of words you [were] hearing, but a form you [were] not seeing; only a voice.
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to you out of the fire. You heard words being spoken, but you saw no form at all, only a voice.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to you from the fire. You heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} speaking, but you did not see any shape. You only heard a voice.

decisions.choice: form: a visible shape or likeness
decisions.reason: The word means the outline or appearance of something that can be seen (Numbers 12:8; Job 4:16). Israel saw fire, but no shape of God.

decisions.choice: sound, voice: one word for both
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the same word for "sound" and "voice". What Israel had of God at Horeb was something heard, not something seen.

decisions.choice: you saw no form: the ground for the ban on images
decisions.reason: Because God showed himself by speaking and not by any visible shape, Israel must not make a shape to stand for him (verses 15-18).

decisions.choice: You heard him speaking
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "the sound of words" was: God speaking.

source.text: וַיַּגֵּ֨ד לָכֶ֜ם אֶת־בְּרִית֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֤ה אֶתְכֶם֙ לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת עֲשֶׂ֖רֶת הַדְּבָרִ֑ים וַֽיִּכְתְּבֵ֔ם עַל־שְׁנֵ֖י לֻח֥וֹת אֲבָנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he declared to you his covenant that he commanded you to do, the ten words; and he wrote them on two tablets of stones.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} declared to you {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded you to do, the ten words; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wrote them on two tablets of stone.
en.B: He made known to you {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant, the Ten Words, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded you to keep, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wrote them on two stone tablets.
en.R: He told you about {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant, the Ten Commandments, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded you to obey them. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wrote them on two flat stones.

decisions.choice: covenant: a binding agreement between God and his people
decisions.reason: A covenant binds two parties by promise and oath. At Horeb God bound himself to Israel and Israel to him, with the Ten Words as its terms (Exodus 24:3-8; 34:28).

decisions.choice: the ten words: the Ten Commandments
decisions.reason: This is the Hebrew name for the commands of Exodus 20:2-17, which Moses repeats in 5:6-21. "Words" here means sayings or commands (Exodus 34:28; Deuteronomy 10:4).

decisions.choice: to do the covenant: to keep its terms
decisions.reason: One "does" a covenant by living by what it requires.

decisions.choice: the ten words / the Ten Words / the Ten Commandments
decisions.reason: As at Exodus 34:28, Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew name; Readable uses the familiar one.

decisions.choice: two flat stones
decisions.reason: Readable says what the tablets were: flat pieces of stone to write on.

source.text: וְאֹתִ֞י צִוָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔וא לְלַמֵּ֣ד אֶתְכֶ֔ם חֻקִּ֖ים וּמִשְׁפָּטִ֑ים לַעֲשֹׂתְכֶ֣ם אֹתָ֔ם בָּאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֛ם עֹבְרִ֥ים שָׁ֖מָּה לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And me commanded Yahweh at the time that to teach you statutes and judgments, for your doing them in the land where you [are] crossing there to take possession of it.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded me at that time to teach you statutes and judgments, for you to do them in the land that you [are] crossing into to take possession of it.
en.B: At that time {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded me to teach you statutes and rulings for you to follow in the land you are crossing over to take possession of.
en.R: At that time {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told me to teach you laws and rules. You are to obey them in the land across the Jordan River that you are going to take possession of.

decisions.choice: me: stressed, Moses' role set beside God's
decisions.reason: "Me" comes first for emphasis. God spoke the Ten Words to all the people himself; the rest of the statutes and rulings he gave through Moses (5:22-31).

decisions.choice: crossing there: crossing the Jordan into the land
decisions.reason: Israel is camped east of the Jordan. To "cross over" is to cross the river into Canaan (verses 21-22, 26).

decisions.choice: across the Jordan River
decisions.reason: Readable names the river that "crossing" refers to.

source.text: וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּ֥ם מְאֹ֖ד לְנַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶ֑ם כִּ֣י לֹ֤א רְאִיתֶם֙ כָּל־תְּמוּנָ֔ה בְּי֗וֹם דִּבֶּ֨ר יְהוָ֧ה אֲלֵיכֶ֛ם בְּחֹרֵ֖ב מִתּ֥וֹךְ הָאֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you shall guard exceedingly your souls, for not you saw any form on [the] day spoke Yahweh to you at Horeb from [the] midst of the fire,

en.L: And you shall guard your souls greatly, for you did not see any form on the day [that] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to you at Horeb from the midst of the fire,
en.B: Be very careful, then, for your own sake. On the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to you at Horeb from the fire, you did not see any shape at all,
en.R: You did not see any shape on the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to you from the fire at Mount Horeb. So be very careful!

decisions.choice: your souls: yourselves
decisions.reason: As in verse 9, "soul" means the self. The warning is to watch over oneself closely.

decisions.choice: you saw no form: the reason for what follows
decisions.reason: God revealed himself at Horeb by voice, not by any visible shape. So no shape may be made to stand for him (verses 16-18).

decisions.choice: You did not see ... So be very careful!
decisions.reason: Readable gives the reason first and the warning after it, which is easier to follow in short sentences.

source.text: פֶּ֨ן־תַּשְׁחִת֔וּן וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֥ם לָכֶ֛ם פֶּ֖סֶל תְּמוּנַ֣ת כָּל־סָ֑מֶל תַּבְנִ֥ית זָכָ֖ר א֥וֹ נְקֵבָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: lest you act corruptly and make for yourselves a carved image, [the] form of any figure, [the] likeness of male or female,

en.L: lest you act corruptly and make for yourselves a carved image, the form of any figure, the likeness of male or female,
en.B: so do not bring ruin on yourselves by making an idol for yourselves in the form of any figure, the likeness of a man or a woman,
en.R: Do not ruin yourselves by making an idol of any shape, whether it looks like a man or a woman,

decisions.choice: act corruptly: ruin yourselves, go to destruction
decisions.reason: The verb means to spoil or destroy. Making an idol would corrupt Israel's worship and bring ruin on the people (9:12; 31:29).

decisions.choice: carved image: an idol shaped by a craftsman
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to carve or hew. It names an idol made of wood, stone or metal (5:8; Exodus 20:4).

decisions.choice: figure: a statue or image
decisions.reason: The word is rare (Ezekiel 8:3, 5). With "form" and "likeness" it shuts out every kind of image, of any shape.

decisions.choice: a man or a woman
decisions.reason: "Male or female" is put in everyday words.

source.text: תַּבְנִ֕ית כָּל־בְּהֵמָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּאָ֑רֶץ תַּבְנִית֙ כָּל־צִפּ֣וֹר כָּנָ֔ף אֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּע֖וּף בַּשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: [the] likeness of any animal that [is] on the earth, [the] likeness of any bird of wing that flies in the heavens,

en.L: the likeness of any animal that [is] on the earth, the likeness of any winged bird that flies in the heavens,
en.B: the likeness of any beast on the earth, the likeness of any winged bird that flies through the sky,
en.R: or like any animal on land or any bird that flies in the sky,

decisions.choice: the list of creatures: the order of creation in reverse
decisions.reason: Verses 16-19 run from humans to land animals, birds, creeping things, fish and then the sun, moon and stars, the creation of Genesis 1:14-27 in reverse. Nothing God made may be worshiped in his place (Romans 1:23).

decisions.choice: animal: any four-footed beast of the land
decisions.reason: The word often means cattle and other domestic animals, but here it stands for every kind of land animal.

decisions.choice: sky
decisions.reason: "The heavens" where birds fly is the sky. Literal keeps "heavens".

source.text: תַּבְנִ֕ית כָּל־רֹמֵ֖שׂ בָּאֲדָמָ֑ה תַּבְנִ֛ית כָּל־דָּגָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־בַּמַּ֖יִם מִתַּ֥חַת לָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: [the] likeness of any creeping [thing] on the ground, [the] likeness of any fish that [is] in the waters under the earth.

en.L: the likeness of anything that creeps on the ground, the likeness of any fish that [is] in the waters under the earth.
en.B: the likeness of anything that creeps on the ground, the likeness of any fish in the waters beneath the land.
en.R: or any creature that crawls on the ground, or any fish in the water.

decisions.choice: creeping thing: small creatures that move close to the ground
decisions.reason: The word covers insects, reptiles and other small animals that creep or crawl (Genesis 1:24-25).

decisions.choice: the waters under the earth: seas, lakes and rivers lower than the land
decisions.reason: The phrase does not mean an underworld. Water lies below the level of the land, and fish live there (5:8; Exodus 20:4).

decisions.choice: in the water
decisions.reason: Readable leaves out "under the earth", which could mislead a young reader; the fish are simply in the water.

source.text: וּפֶן־תִּשָּׂ֨א עֵינֶ֜יךָ הַשָּׁמַ֗יְמָה וְֽ֠רָאִיתָ אֶת־הַשֶּׁ֨מֶשׁ וְאֶת־הַיָּרֵ֜חַ וְאֶת־הַכּֽוֹכָבִ֗ים כֹּ֚ל צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְנִדַּחְתָּ֛ וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִ֥יתָ לָהֶ֖ם וַעֲבַדְתָּ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר חָלַ֜ק יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ אֹתָ֔ם לְכֹל֙ הָֽעַמִּ֔ים תַּ֖חַת כָּל־הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And lest you lift up your eyes to the heavens and see the sun and the moon and the stars, all [the] host of the heavens, and you be drawn away and bow down to them and serve them, which has allotted Yahweh your God to all the peoples under all the heavens.

en.L: And lest you lift up your eyes to the heavens and see the sun and the moon and the stars, all the host of the heavens, and you be drawn away and bow down to them and serve them, which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has allotted to all the peoples under all the heavens.
en.B: Do not raise your eyes to the sky and, seeing the sun, the moon, and the stars, all the host of heaven, be drawn away to bow down to them and serve them. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has allotted them to all the peoples under the whole sky.
en.R: And when you look up into the sky and see the sun, moon, and stars, do not be tempted to bow down and worship them. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given them to all the peoples everywhere under the sky.

decisions.choice: the host of the heavens: the sun, moon and stars, seen as an army
decisions.reason: "Host" means an army or a great company. The heavenly bodies were counted as a vast host, and many nations worshiped them as gods (17:3; 2 Kings 21:3, 5).

decisions.choice: drawn away: pulled aside, led astray
decisions.reason: The verb means to be pushed or drawn away from the right path. The beauty of the sky could lure Israel into worshiping what God made.

decisions.choice: allotted to all the peoples: given to all nations for their use, or left to them as their gods
alternatives: given to all peoples as lights
left to the nations as objects of their worship
decisions.reason: The verb means to divide out shares. It may mean that God gave the sun, moon and stars to all peoples alike, as lights (Genesis 1:14-18), so they are no god of Israel's. Or it may mean that God left the nations to worship them, while he took Israel as his own (verse 20; 29:25; 32:8-9). The words allow both.

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: Readable says "worship" for "serve", which here means serving as gods.

decisions.choice: Do not raise your eyes ... / do not be tempted
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "lest" into a direct warning and give what God has done with the sky a sentence of its own.

source.text: וְאֶתְכֶם֙ לָקַ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה וַיּוֹצִ֥א אֶתְכֶ֛ם מִכּ֥וּר הַבַּרְזֶ֖ל מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם לִהְי֥וֹת ל֛וֹ לְעַ֥ם נַחֲלָ֖ה כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: But you took Yahweh and brought out you from the furnace of iron, from Egypt, to be for him a people of inheritance, as [this] day this.

en.L: But you {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} took, and brought you out of the furnace of iron, out of Egypt, to be a people of inheritance for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, as [it is] this day.
en.B: But you are the ones {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} took and brought out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own people, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} inheritance, as you are today.
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} took you and rescued you from Egypt, where you suffered as if you were in a blazing furnace. He did this so that you would be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} very own people, as you are today.

decisions.choice: But you: Israel set against the peoples of verse 19
decisions.reason: "You" comes first for emphasis. The nations have the sky; Israel the LORD took for himself.

decisions.choice: the iron furnace: Egypt as a place of fierce suffering
decisions.reason: A furnace for smelting iron burned very hot. The picture is of the harsh slavery of Egypt, and perhaps of testing that refines (1 Kings 8:51; Jeremiah 11:4).

decisions.choice: a people of inheritance: a people who belong to God as his own possession
decisions.reason: The word for inheritance names family property handed down and kept for good. Israel is God's lasting possession (9:26, 29; 32:9).

decisions.choice: But you are the ones ...
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the stress on "you" with "you are the ones".

decisions.choice: where you suffered as if you were in a blazing furnace
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the iron furnace.

source.text: וַֽיהוָ֥ה הִתְאַנֶּף־בִּ֖יעַל־דִּבְרֵיכֶ֑ם וַיִּשָּׁבַ֗ע לְבִלְתִּ֤י עָבְרִי֙ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וּלְבִלְתִּי־בֹא֙ אֶל־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַטּוֹבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לְךָ֖ נַחֲלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Yahweh was angry with me on account of your words, and he swore that not I would cross the Jordan and not go into the land good that Yahweh your God [is] giving to you [as] an inheritance.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was angry with me on account of your words, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore that I would not cross the Jordan and would not go into the good land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God [is] giving you [as] an inheritance.
en.B: Because of you, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was angry with me and swore that I would not go over the Jordan or come into the good land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you as an inheritance.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was angry with me because of you. He swore that I would never cross the Jordan River and go into the good land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you to keep as your own.

decisions.choice: on account of your words: because of you, because of what you did
decisions.reason: "Words" can mean matters or affairs. Moses says, as in 1:37 and 3:26, that it was because of the people that he too may not enter.

decisions.choice: the LORD was angry and swore: the judgment at Meribah
decisions.reason: Numbers 20:2-13 tells how, when the people complained for water, Moses and Aaron did not honor God as holy, and God said they would not bring the people into the land. Deuteronomy stresses the people's part in it.

decisions.choice: inheritance: a lasting family possession
decisions.reason: The land is given as property to be handed down from generation to generation, as in verse 20.

decisions.choice: because of you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom; Literal keeps "on account of your words".

source.text: כִּ֣י אָנֹכִ֥י מֵת֙ בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את אֵינֶ֥נִּי עֹבֵ֖ר אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וְאַתֶּם֙ עֹֽבְרִ֔ים וִֽירִשְׁתֶּ֕ם אֶת־הָאָ֥רֶץ הַטּוֹבָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: For I [am] dying in the land this; not I [am] crossing the Jordan; but you [are] crossing and will take possession of the land good this.

en.L: For I [am] dying in this land; I [am] not crossing the Jordan; but you [are] crossing over, and you will take possession of this good land.
en.B: I must die here in this land and not cross the Jordan, but you are going over, and you will take possession of this good land.
en.R: I am going to die here in this land. I will not cross the Jordan River. But you will go across and take possession of that good land.

decisions.choice: dying ... crossing: what is about to happen
decisions.reason: The verbs describe events close at hand: Moses will soon die (34:5), and the people will soon cross.

decisions.choice: this land: Moab, east of the Jordan, where Moses is speaking
decisions.reason: The first "this land" is where Moses stands. The second, "this good land", is Canaan across the river, the land everyone is thinking of.

decisions.choice: that good land
decisions.reason: Readable says "that" for the land across the river, so readers do not confuse it with the land where Moses will die.

source.text: הִשָּׁמְר֣וּ לָכֶ֗ם פֶּֽן־תִּשְׁכְּחוּ֙ אֶת־בְּרִ֤ית יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּרַ֖ת עִמָּכֶ֑ם וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֨ם לָכֶ֥ם פֶּ֨סֶל֙ תְּמ֣וּנַת כֹּ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוְּךָ֖ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Take heed to yourselves lest you forget [the] covenant of Yahweh your God that he made with you, and make for yourselves a carved image, [the] form of anything that commanded you Yahweh your God.

en.L: Take heed to yourselves, lest you forget the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made with you, and make for yourselves a carved image, the form of anything that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has commanded you [not to make].
en.B: Watch yourselves, so that you do not forget the covenant {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God made with you by making yourselves an idol shaped like anything at all, which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has forbidden you.
en.R: Be careful! Do not forget the covenant {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God made with you. Do not make an idol shaped like anything at all. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has told you not to do that.

decisions.choice: that the LORD commanded you: what he commanded you about, that is, forbade
decisions.reason: The clause refers to the command against images (verse 16; 5:8). What God "commanded" concerning them is that they must not be made.

decisions.choice: made a covenant: literally "cut" a covenant
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is "cut", perhaps from the cutting of animals in covenant rites (Genesis 15:9-18). It is the usual way to say "make a covenant".

decisions.choice: forgetting the covenant and making an image: one sin, not two
decisions.reason: To make an image is to forget the covenant, whose first terms forbid other gods and images (5:7-10).

decisions.choice: which the LORD your God has forbidden you / told you not to do that
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say outright that the command was a prohibition. Literal keeps "commanded".

source.text: כִּ֚י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֵ֥שׁ אֹכְלָ֖ה ה֑וּא אֵ֖ל קַנָּֽא׃פ

records.literal_gloss: For Yahweh your God, a fire consuming he [is], a God jealous.

en.L: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] a consuming fire, a jealous God.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is a devouring fire, a God who is jealous.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is like a fire that burns up everything. He is a jealous God, who wants you to worship only {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: a consuming fire: his holiness destroys what sets itself against him
decisions.reason: God appeared at Horeb in fire (verses 11-12). The fire that showed his presence is also a picture of his judgment on those who turn from him (9:3; Exodus 24:17; Hebrews 12:29).

decisions.choice: jealous: zealous for the loyalty that belongs to him alone
decisions.reason: The word describes the passion of one who will not share what is rightly his, like a husband's claim on his wife's faithfulness. It is not petty envy but God's demand for undivided worship (5:9; Exodus 20:5; 34:14).

decisions.choice: who wants you to worship only him
decisions.reason: Readable explains what God's jealousy is about, so young readers do not take it as envy.

decisions.choice: like a fire
decisions.reason: Readable marks the fire as a picture.

source.text: כִּֽי־תוֹלִ֤יד בָּנִים֙ וּבְנֵ֣י בָנִ֔ים וְנוֹשַׁנְתֶּ֖ם בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְהִשְׁחַתֶּ֗ם וַעֲשִׂ֤יתֶם פֶּ֨סֶל֙ תְּמ֣וּנַת כֹּ֔ל וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֥ם הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה־אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לְהַכְעִיסֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: When you father children and children of children, and you have grown old in the land, and you act corruptly and make a carved image, [the] form of anything, and do the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh your God to provoke him,

en.L: When you father {{gender:children|sons}} and {{gender:children's children|sons' sons}}, and you have grown old in the land, and you act corruptly and make a carved image, the form of anything, and do the evil in the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, to provoke {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to anger,
en.B: When you have had {{gender:children|sons}} and {{gender:grandchildren|grandsons}} and have grown old in the land, and you act corruptly and make an idol in the form of anything, doing what is evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and provoking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to anger,
en.R: In the future you will have {{gender:children|sons}} and {{gender:grandchildren|grandsons}}, and you will live in the land a long time. Then you might ruin yourselves by making an idol of some kind. You would be doing what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God says is evil, and you would make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} angry.

decisions.choice: grown old: settled long in the land, and grown used to it
decisions.reason: The verb means to become old or long-established. After generations in the land, the danger is that the memory of Horeb fades (6:10-12; 8:11-14).

decisions.choice: when: a real danger Moses sees ahead
decisions.reason: The sentence describes what may happen and what will follow if it does. Later Moses speaks of it as what will happen (31:16-21, 29).

decisions.choice: do the evil in the eyes of the LORD: do what he judges evil
decisions.reason: "In the eyes of" means in someone's judgment. The phrase becomes the standard verdict on Israel's idolatry (Judges 2:11; 2 Kings 17:17).

decisions.choice: grandchildren
decisions.reason: As in verse 9: "children's children" is "grandchildren".

source.text: הַעִידֹתִי֩ בָכֶ֨ם הַיּ֜וֹם אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם וְאֶת־הָאָ֗רֶץ כִּֽי־אָבֹ֣ד תֹּאבֵדוּן֮ מַהֵר֒ מֵעַ֣ל הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַתֶּ֜ם עֹבְרִ֧ים אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֛ן שָׁ֖מָּה לְרִשְׁתָּ֑הּ לֹֽא־תַאֲרִיכֻ֤ן יָמִים֙ עָלֶ֔יהָ כִּ֥י הִשָּׁמֵ֖ד תִּשָּׁמֵדֽוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: I call as witness against you today the heavens and the earth, that perishing you will perish quickly from on the land where you [are] crossing the Jordan there to take possession of it; not you will prolong days on it, for being destroyed you will be destroyed.

en.L: I call the heavens and the earth to witness against you today that you will surely perish quickly from the land that you [are] crossing the Jordan into to take possession of it. You will not prolong [your] days on it, for you will surely be destroyed.
en.B: Today I call heaven and earth to testify against you: you will soon be wiped out from the land you are crossing the Jordan to take possession of. You will not live long in it; you will be utterly destroyed.
en.R: Today I am calling the sky and the earth to be witnesses against you. If you do that, you will soon be gone from the land you are crossing the Jordan River to take possession of. You will not live there long. You will be completely destroyed.

decisions.choice: heaven and earth as witnesses: the witnesses of a covenant
decisions.reason: Treaties of the time named witnesses who would see that the terms were kept. Moses calls on heaven and earth, which last from generation to generation (30:19; 31:28; 32:1; Isaiah 1:2).

decisions.choice: perishing you will perish ... being destroyed you will be destroyed: certainty
decisions.reason: Hebrew repeats the verb to make a statement certain and strong. The loss of the land is sure if they turn to idols.

decisions.choice: prolong days: live long
decisions.reason: To "lengthen days" on the land is to live long there and keep it (verse 40; 5:33).

decisions.choice: If you do that
decisions.reason: Readable states the condition carried over from verse 25.

source.text: וְהֵפִ֧יץ יְהוָ֛ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם בָּעַמִּ֑ים וְנִשְׁאַרְתֶּם֙ מְתֵ֣י מִסְפָּ֔ר בַּגּוֹיִ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְנַהֵ֧ג יְהוָ֛ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם שָֽׁמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will scatter Yahweh you among the peoples, and you will be left men of number among the nations where will drive Yahweh you there.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will scatter you among the peoples, and you will be left few in number among the nations where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will drive you.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will scatter you among the peoples, and you will be left a small number among the nations to which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} drives you.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will scatter you among other nations. Only a few of you will be left alive in the places where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sends you.

decisions.choice: men of number: few, so few they could be counted
decisions.reason: People who can be counted are few (Genesis 34:30; Jeremiah 44:28). The people once as many as the stars (1:10) would be reduced to a remnant.

decisions.choice: scatter: exile as the judgment of the covenant
decisions.reason: Being driven from the land and scattered among nations is one of the covenant curses (28:36, 64), and it came about in the exiles to Assyria and Babylon (2 Kings 17:6; 25:21).

decisions.choice: few in number
decisions.reason: The Hebrew idiom is put in words English can follow even at Literal.

source.text: וַעֲבַדְתֶּם־שָׁ֣ם אֱלֹהִ֔ים מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יְדֵ֣י אָדָ֑ם עֵ֣ץ וָאֶ֔בֶן אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־יִרְאוּן֙ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁמְע֔וּן וְלֹ֥א יֹֽאכְל֖וּן וְלֹ֥א יְרִיחֻֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will serve there gods, [the] work of [the] hands of man, wood and stone, which not see and not hear and not eat and not smell.

en.L: And there you will serve gods, the work of human hands, wood and stone, which do not see and do not hear and do not eat and do not smell.
en.B: There you will serve gods that human hands have made, wood and stone, gods that neither see nor hear, neither eat nor smell.
en.R: There you will worship gods that people have made out of wood and stone. These gods cannot see, hear, eat, or smell.

decisions.choice: serving lifeless gods: the punishment matches the sin
decisions.reason: Those who wanted to make images will end up serving images in exile. The idols have none of the senses of living beings, unlike the God who speaks and hears (Psalm 115:4-7; 135:15-17).

decisions.choice: man: human beings
decisions.reason: The word means humankind. The gods are things people have made.

decisions.choice: neither see nor hear / cannot see
decisions.reason: "Do not see" means they are not able to. Balanced says "neither ... nor" and Readable "cannot".

source.text: וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּ֥ם מִשָּׁ֛ם אֶת־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ וּמָצָ֑אתָ כִּ֣י תִדְרְשֶׁ֔נּוּ בְּכָל־לְבָבְךָ֖ וּבְכָל־נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will seek from there Yahweh your God, and you will find, when you search for him with all your heart and with all your soul.

en.L: And from there you will seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and you will find [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], when you search for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all your heart and with all your soul.
en.B: But from there you will seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and you will find {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, if you search after {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all your heart and with all your soul.
en.R: But even there you will look for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. And you will find {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} if you look for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all your heart and with all your being.

decisions.choice: when: the condition for finding him
decisions.reason: The word can mean "when" or "if" or "because". God will be found by those who seek him wholeheartedly (Jeremiah 29:13).

decisions.choice: with all your heart and all your soul: with the whole person
decisions.reason: Heart is mind and will; soul is the self, one's very life. Together they mean with everything one is (6:5; 10:12).

decisions.choice: seek, search for: two verbs for seeking God
decisions.reason: The first means to look for; the second, to inquire after, to seek earnestly. The repetition stresses the seeking.

decisions.choice: But
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the turn from exile to hope with "But".

decisions.choice: being
decisions.reason: Readable says "being" for "soul", the whole self, since "soul" can suggest only an inner part of a person. Literal and Balanced keep "soul".

source.text: בַּצַּ֣ר לְךָ֔ וּמְצָא֕וּךָ כֹּ֖ל הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה בְּאַחֲרִית֙ הַיָּמִ֔ים וְשַׁבְתָּ֙ עַד־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ וְשָׁמַעְתָּ֖ בְּקֹלֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: In your distress, and find you all the things these in [the] latter end of the days, and you will return to Yahweh your God and listen to his voice.

en.L: In your distress, when all these things have found you in the latter end of the days, you will return to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and listen to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice.
en.B: In your distress, when all these things have overtaken you in the days to come, you will turn back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Someday you will be in deep trouble, and all these things will happen to you. Then you will come back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: the latter end of the days: the time to come, the future
decisions.reason: The phrase points ahead to a later time (31:29; Genesis 49:1). Here it is the time after the exile has come; it need not mean the end of the world.

decisions.choice: return: turn back to God, repent
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn around. Turning back to God after going after other gods is repentance (30:2, 8-10).

decisions.choice: listen to his voice: obey him
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice in Hebrew is to do what they say.

decisions.choice: obey him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom; Literal keeps "listen to his voice".

source.text: כִּ֣י אֵ֤ל רַחוּם֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ לֹ֥א יַרְפְּךָ֖ וְלֹ֣א יַשְׁחִיתֶ֑ךָ וְלֹ֤א יִשְׁכַּח֙ אֶת־בְּרִ֣ית אֲבֹתֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֖ע לָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For a God compassionate [is] Yahweh your God; not he will let you go, and not destroy you, and not forget the covenant of your fathers that he swore to them.

en.L: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God [is] a compassionate God; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not let you go, nor destroy you, nor forget the covenant of your fathers that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to them.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is a God of compassion. He will not let you go or bring you to ruin, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not forget the covenant {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to your ancestors.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is a God who shows mercy. He will not leave you on your own or destroy you. He will not forget the covenant {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised your ancestors with an oath.

decisions.choice: compassionate: tender, full of mercy
decisions.reason: The word is related to the word for womb, and speaks of the tender love of a mother for her child. God names himself so in Exodus 34:6.

decisions.choice: let you go: drop you, leave you without help
decisions.reason: The verb means to let go one's hold or let sink. God will not let go of his people even in exile (31:6, 8).

decisions.choice: the covenant he swore to the fathers: the promises to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
decisions.reason: God bound himself by oath to give Abraham's descendants the land and to be their God (Genesis 15:18; 17:7-8; 22:16-18; 26:3). His faithfulness to that oath is the ground of hope for exiles.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

source.text: כִּ֣י שְׁאַל־נָא֩ לְיָמִ֨ים רִֽאשֹׁנִ֜ים אֲשֶׁר־הָי֣וּ לְפָנֶ֗יךָ לְמִן־הַיּוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁר֩ בָּרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀אָדָם֙ עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ וּלְמִקְצֵ֥ה הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְעַד־קְצֵ֣ה הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם הֲנִֽהְיָ֗ה כַּדָּבָ֤ר הַגָּדוֹל֙ הַזֶּ֔ה א֖וֹ הֲנִשְׁמַ֥ע כָּמֹֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For ask, please, about [the] days former that were before you, from the day that created God man on the earth, and from [the] end of the heavens and to [the] end of the heavens: has there been [anything] like the thing great this, or has been heard [anything] like it?

en.L: For ask now about the former days that were before you, from the day that God created humankind on the earth, and from [one] end of the heavens to [the other] end of the heavens: has [anything] been like this great thing, or has [anything] like it been heard?
en.B: Go ahead and inquire about the past, the days that came before you, back to the day God created human beings on the earth. Search from one edge of the sky to the other. Has anything this great ever taken place? Has anything like it ever been heard?
en.R: Think about the past, long before you were born. Go all the way back to the day God made people on the earth. Search the whole world, from one end of the sky to the other. Has anything this great ever happened before? Has anyone ever heard of anything like it?

decisions.choice: the day God created humankind: the creation of Genesis 1
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in Genesis 1:1, 27 for God's creating. Moses invites a search through all of history since then.

decisions.choice: from one end of the heavens to the other: everywhere under the sky
decisions.reason: The sky was pictured as a vault with edges at the horizon. From end to end means the whole world (30:4).

decisions.choice: has there been ...? : questions that expect "never"
decisions.reason: Like verses 7-8, the questions make a point: nothing like this has ever happened or been heard of.

decisions.choice: Think about ... Search the whole world
decisions.reason: "Ask" here means to look into the past and the whole world for anything comparable. Readable says that directly.

source.text: הֲשָׁ֣מַֽע עָם֩ ק֨וֹל אֱלֹהִ֜ים מְדַבֵּ֧ר מִתּוֹךְ־הָאֵ֛שׁ כַּאֲשֶׁר־שָׁמַ֥עְתָּ אַתָּ֖ה וַיֶּֽחִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Has heard a people [the] voice of God speaking from [the] midst of the fire, as have heard you, and lived?

en.L: Has a people heard the voice of God speaking from the midst of the fire, as you yourself have heard, and lived?
en.B: Did any people ever hear the voice of God speaking from the midst of fire, as you heard it, and live?
en.R: Has any other nation ever heard God speaking from the middle of a fire, as you did, and still lived?

decisions.choice: God: Israel's God, or any god
decisions.reason: The word can mean God or a god. Here it most likely means God himself, who spoke at Horeb (5:26 "the living God"); the question asks whether any other people has had this experience.

decisions.choice: and lived: hearing God directly was thought to bring death
decisions.reason: The people at Horeb feared they would die if they heard God's voice again (5:24-26; Exodus 20:19). That they lived is part of the wonder.

decisions.choice: any other
decisions.reason: Readable adds "other" to make clear that Israel is the one people that has. Literal and Balanced keep the open question.

source.text: א֣וֹ׀הֲנִסָּ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֗ים לָ֠בוֹא לָקַ֨חַת ל֣וֹ גוֹי֮ מִקֶּ֣רֶב גּוֹי֒ בְּמַסֹּת֩ בְּאֹתֹ֨ת וּבְמוֹפְתִ֜ים וּבְמִלְחָמָ֗ה וּבְיָ֤ד חֲזָקָה֙ וּבִזְר֣וֹעַ נְטוּיָ֔ה וּבְמוֹרָאִ֖ים גְּדֹלִ֑ים כְּ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֨ה לָכֶ֜ם יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֛ם בְּמִצְרַ֖יִם לְעֵינֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Or has tried a god to go to take for himself a nation from [the] midst of a nation, by trials, by signs and by wonders, and by war, and by a hand strong and by an arm outstretched, and by terrors great, like all that did for you Yahweh your God in Egypt before your eyes?

en.L: Or has a god tried to go and take for himself a nation from the midst of [another] nation, by trials, by signs and by wonders, and by war, and by a strong hand and by an outstretched arm, and by great terrors, like all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?
en.B: Or did any god ever attempt to come and take one nation for himself from within another, by trials, signs and wonders, by war, by a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and by great terrors, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God did for you in Egypt while you watched?
en.R: Has any other god ever tried to take one nation out from inside another nation and make it his own? {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God did that for you in Egypt, and you saw it happen. He sent trials and signs and miracles. He fought a war. He used {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power and strength and did terrifying things.

decisions.choice: a god: any so-called god of the nations
decisions.reason: Here the word means "a god", since its verb and "for himself" are singular and the question compares the LORD with others: has any god ever done such a thing?

decisions.choice: trials: tests, the plagues that put Pharaoh to the test
decisions.reason: The word means testings. The plagues tested Pharaoh and Egypt again and again (7:19; 29:2 in Hebrew numbering).

decisions.choice: a strong hand and an outstretched arm: God's power in action
decisions.reason: The hand and arm are pictures of strength put to work. The phrase recalls the exodus (5:15; 26:8; Exodus 6:6).

decisions.choice: terrors: awe-inspiring deeds that cause fear
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "fear". It names deeds so great that those who see them are struck with awe (26:8; 34:12).

decisions.choice: Has any other god ...? The LORD your God did that for you ...
decisions.reason: Readable asks the question first and then lists what God did in separate short sentences.

decisions.choice: signs and miracles
decisions.reason: "Wonders" in Readable is "miracles", acts beyond what is natural.

source.text: אַתָּה֙ הָרְאֵ֣תָ לָדַ֔עַת כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה ה֣וּא הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים אֵ֥ין ע֖וֹד מִלְבַדּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: You, you were shown to know that Yahweh, he [is] the God; there is no other besides him.

en.L: You were shown [this] so that you would know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] the God; there is no other besides {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: You were shown all this so that you would know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is God, and that there is no other besides {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} showed you these things so that you would know that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the true God. There is no other God but {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: you were shown: God made you see
decisions.reason: The verb is passive: Israel was made to see. God is the one who showed them these things, and the purpose was knowledge.

decisions.choice: the God: God in the full sense, the only true God
decisions.reason: With the article, the word means "the God", the one who truly is God (verse 39; 1 Kings 18:39).

decisions.choice: there is no other besides him: the LORD alone is God
decisions.reason: The verse denies that any other god is truly God (verse 39; 32:39; Isaiah 45:5-6).

decisions.choice: The LORD showed you ... the true God
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD as the one who showed them, and says "true" for the force of "the God".

source.text: מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם הִשְׁמִֽיעֲךָ֥ אֶת־קֹל֖וֹ לְיַסְּרֶ֑ךָּ וְעַל־הָאָ֗רֶץ הֶרְאֲךָ֙ אֶת־אִשּׁ֣וֹ הַגְּדוֹלָ֔ה וּדְבָרָ֥יו שָׁמַ֖עְתָּ מִתּ֥וֹךְ הָאֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: From the heavens he made you hear his voice to discipline you, and on the earth he showed you his fire great, and his words you heard from [the] midst of the fire.

en.L: From the heavens {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made you hear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice to discipline you, and on the earth {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed you {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great fire, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words you heard from the midst of the fire.
en.B: He let you hear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice from heaven to instruct you, and on earth {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} let you see {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great fire; out of that fire you heard {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words.
en.R: He spoke to you from heaven so that you would learn from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. On earth {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed you {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great fire, and you heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} speak from the fire.

decisions.choice: discipline: train and correct, like a father
decisions.reason: The verb means to instruct by correction, as a parent trains a child (8:5). God's voice from heaven taught Israel who he is and how to live.

decisions.choice: from heaven ... on earth: God above all, yet present to speak
decisions.reason: God's voice came from heaven and his fire was seen on the mountain. He is not bound to any place on earth, and yet he came near (verse 39; Exodus 20:22).

decisions.choice: instruct / learn from him
decisions.reason: Balanced says "instruct" and Readable "learn from him", since "discipline" can suggest only punishment.

source.text: וְתַ֗חַת כִּ֤י אָהַב֙ אֶת־אֲבֹתֶ֔יךָ וַיִּבְחַ֥ר בְּזַרְע֖וֹ אַחֲרָ֑יו וַיּוֹצִֽאֲךָ֧ בְּפָנָ֛יו בְּכֹח֥וֹ הַגָּדֹ֖ל מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And because he loved your fathers and chose his offspring after him, and he brought you out by his presence, by his power great, from Egypt,

en.L: And because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved your fathers and chose his offspring after him, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought you out with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence, with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power, from Egypt,
en.B: He loved your ancestors and chose their descendants after them, and for that reason {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} brought you out of Egypt with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} loved your ancestors and chose their descendants. That is why {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} went with you and brought you out of Egypt by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power.

decisions.choice: his offspring after him: the descendants of the fathers
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "his" and "him", singular, though "fathers" is plural; the singular may think of Abraham, or of the fathers as one. The Samaritan Pentateuch and the ancient Greek and Syriac versions have "their offspring after them". Either way the meaning is the descendants of the fathers, that is, Israel (10:15).

decisions.choice: by his presence: in person
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is "by his face". God did not send someone else; he himself went with Israel (Exodus 33:14-15; Isaiah 63:9).

decisions.choice: because he loved and chose: God's choice rests on his love
decisions.reason: Israel was not chosen for its size or merit but because God loved its fathers (7:7-8; 10:15).

decisions.choice: their descendants after them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "their" so that the words are not taken to mean God's offspring. Literal keeps the singular.

decisions.choice: for that reason he himself / That is why he himself went with you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put "because" as a clause of reason after the fact and explain "by his presence" as God himself; Readable also names the LORD.

source.text: לְהוֹרִ֗ישׁ גּוֹיִ֛ם גְּדֹלִ֧ים וַעֲצֻמִ֛ים מִמְּךָ֖ מִפָּנֶ֑יךָ לַהֲבִֽיאֲךָ֗ לָֽתֶת־לְךָ֧ אֶת־אַרְצָ֛ם נַחֲלָ֖ה כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: to dispossess nations greater and mightier than you from before you, to bring you in, to give to you their land [as] an inheritance, as [this] day this.

en.L: to dispossess nations greater and mightier than you from before you, to bring you in, to give you their land [as] an inheritance, as [it is] this day.
en.B: driving out ahead of you nations bigger and mightier than you, to bring you in and give you their land as your inheritance, as it now is.
en.R: He did this in order to drive out nations that were bigger and stronger than you. He brought you in to give you their land to keep as your own, as is happening today.

decisions.choice: dispossess: drive out the nations and take their place
decisions.reason: The verb used for taking possession of the land, in this form, means to make others lose possession: to drive them out (7:1; 9:1-5).

decisions.choice: as it is this day: already begun east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Israel already holds the lands of Sihon and Og (2:24-3:17; verses 46-47), a first share of the gift.

decisions.choice: He did this in order to
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and names the purpose, since its verse 37 ended with a full stop.

source.text: וְיָדַעְתָּ֣ הַיּ֗וֹם וַהֲשֵׁבֹתָ֮ אֶל־לְבָבֶךָ֒ כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ ה֣וּא הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים בַּשָּׁמַ֣יִם מִמַּ֔עַל וְעַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ מִתָּ֑חַת אֵ֖ין עֽוֹד׃

records.literal_gloss: And you shall know today and bring back to your heart that Yahweh, he [is] the God in the heavens above and on the earth beneath; there is no other.

en.L: And you shall know today, and bring [it] back to your heart, that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] the God in the heavens above and on the earth beneath; there is no other.
en.B: So know this today, and take it to heart: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is God in the heavens above and on the earth below, and there is no other.
en.R: So today, understand this and never forget it: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is God in heaven above and on the earth below. There is no other God.

decisions.choice: bring back to your heart: take to heart, keep in mind
decisions.reason: To bring something back to the heart is to think it over and let it shape one's thinking (30:1; 1 Kings 8:47).

decisions.choice: God in heaven and on earth; there is no other
decisions.reason: As in verse 35. The God who spoke from heaven and showed his fire on earth (verse 36) rules in both; no other god has any place.

decisions.choice: There is no other God
decisions.reason: Readable says what "no other" means.

source.text: וְשָׁמַרְתָּ֞ אֶת־חֻקָּ֣יו וְאֶת־מִצְוֺתָ֗יו אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֤י מְצַוְּךָ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם אֲשֶׁר֙ יִיטַ֣ב לְךָ֔ וּלְבָנֶ֖יךָ אַחֲרֶ֑יךָ וּלְמַ֨עַן תַּאֲרִ֤יךְ יָמִים֙ עַל־הַ֣אֲדָמָ֔האֲשֶׁ֨ר יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לְךָ֖ כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And you shall keep his statutes and his commandments that I [am] commanding you today, that it may go well for you and for your children after you, and so that you may prolong days on the land that Yahweh your God [is] giving to you all the days.

en.L: And you shall keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments that I [am] commanding you today, so that it may go well with you and with your {{gender:children|sons}} after you, and so that you may prolong [your] days on the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God [is] giving you for all time."
en.B: Keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments that I command you today, and things will go well for you and for your {{gender:children|sons}} after you, and you will have long life in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you for all time."
en.R: Obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws and commands that I am giving you today. Then things will go well for you and for your {{gender:children|sons}} after you. And you will live a long time in the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you to keep forever."

decisions.choice: all the days: the land given for all time, or a long life there for always
alternatives: so that you may live long on the land ... for all time
decisions.reason: "All the days" may go with "giving": the land is given for good. Or it may go with "prolong days": Israel may live there always. The Hebrew order puts it after "giving to you", and that is the reading followed here.

decisions.choice: that it may go well with you: that you may prosper
decisions.reason: A common promise in Deuteronomy (5:16, 29; 6:3, 18): obedience brings a good life in the land for the people and their children.

decisions.choice: the end of Moses' first speech
decisions.reason: The speech that began at 1:6 ends here. Verses 41-49 are the narrator's words.

decisions.choice: the closing quotation mark
decisions.reason: The quotation mark opened at 1:6 closes at the end of this verse, where Moses' first speech ends.

source.text: אָ֣ז יַבְדִּ֤יל מֹשֶׁה֙ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ עָרִ֔ים בְּעֵ֖בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן מִזְרְחָ֖ה שָֽׁמֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: Then set apart Moses three cities across the Jordan toward [the] rising of [the] sun,

en.L: Then Moses set apart three cities across the Jordan, toward the rising of the sun,
en.B: Then Moses set apart three cities across the Jordan, to the east,
en.R: Then Moses chose three towns on the east side of the Jordan River.

decisions.choice: Then: the narrator speaks again, after Moses' speech
decisions.reason: Moses' first speech ends at verse 40. "Then" loosely ties the next event to that time, in the plains of Moab.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan toward the sunrise: east of the river
decisions.reason: "Across the Jordan" is said from the viewpoint of the land west of it, as at 1:1 and 1:5; "toward the rising of the sun" makes plain that the east side is meant here.

decisions.choice: three cities set apart: the cities of refuge east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: God commanded six cities of refuge, three on each side of the Jordan (Numbers 35:9-15). Moses names the eastern three here; the western three are set apart later (19:1-10; Joshua 20:7-8).

decisions.choice: towns on the east side of the Jordan River
decisions.reason: Readable says "towns", as it does for the cities of refuge, and puts the direction in plain words. It ends the sentence here and goes on in verse 42.

source.text: לָנֻ֨ס שָׁ֜מָּה רוֹצֵ֗חַ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִרְצַ֤ח אֶת־רֵעֵ֨הוּ֙ בִּבְלִי־דַ֔עַת וְה֛וּא לֹא־שֹׂנֵ֥א ל֖וֹ מִתְּמ֣וֹל שִׁלְשׁ֑וֹם וְנָ֗ס אֶל־אַחַ֛ת מִן־הֶעָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖ל וָחָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: for fleeing there of a killer who kills his neighbor without knowledge, and he [was] not hating him from yesterday [and the] third day, and he will flee to one of the cities these and live:

en.L: for a killer to flee there, who kills his neighbor without knowing, and he [was] not hating him in time past; and he may flee to one of these cities and live:
en.B: so that anyone who had killed a neighbor by accident, without having been an enemy beforehand, could flee there. By fleeing to one of these cities, that person could stay alive.
en.R: If someone killed another person by accident, and had not hated that person before, the killer could run to one of these towns and stay alive.

decisions.choice: without knowledge: without meaning to, by accident
decisions.reason: The killing was not intended. The law of 19:4-6 uses the same words and gives the example of an axe head that flies off and kills a companion.

decisions.choice: from yesterday and the third day: before, in time past
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "yesterday and the day before" for any time before. The killer had no past hatred for the one who died, which shows it was not murder (19:4, 6, 11).

decisions.choice: a killer, he: anyone who kills, man or woman
decisions.reason: The law is written with masculine words, as Hebrew laws usually are, but it covers anyone who killed by accident (Numbers 35:15).

decisions.choice: live: be safe from the avenger of blood
decisions.reason: The city protected the killer from the dead person's relative who would avenge the death (19:6; Numbers 35:12, 19).

decisions.choice: anyone who had killed a neighbor / someone
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use words that are already inclusive; Literal keeps the masculine words of the Hebrew.

source.text: אֶת־בֶּ֧צֶר בַּמִּדְבָּ֛ר בְּאֶ֥רֶץ הַמִּישֹׁ֖ר לָרֻֽאוּבֵנִ֑יוְאֶת־רָאמֹ֤ת בַּגִּלְעָד֙ לַגָּדִ֔י וְאֶת־גּוֹלָ֥ן בַּבָּשָׁ֖ן לַֽמְנַשִּֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: Bezer in the wilderness in [the] land of the plateau for the Reubenites, and Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.

en.L: Bezer in the wilderness, in the land of the plateau, for the Reubenites; and Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.
en.B: They were Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau, for the Reubenites; Ramoth in Gilead, for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan, for the Manassites.
en.R: The towns were Bezer in the desert on the high plain, for the tribe of Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead, for the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan, for the tribe of Manasseh.

decisions.choice: the plateau: the high tableland north of the Arnon
decisions.reason: The word means level ground. It names the high plain of Moab east of the Dead Sea (3:10; Joshua 13:9, 16).

decisions.choice: the Manassites: the half-tribe of Manasseh east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Only half of Manasseh settled east of the Jordan, in Gilead and Bashan (3:13).

decisions.choice: Bezer, Ramoth, Golan: one city in each eastern tribe, from south to north
decisions.reason: The three cities run from south to north, so that every part of the land east of the Jordan was within reach of a refuge (Joshua 20:8; 21:36-38).

decisions.choice: They were / The towns were
decisions.reason: The Hebrew list follows the colon of verse 42; Balanced and Readable, which ended verse 42 with a full stop, begin the list with a short clause.

decisions.choice: the tribe of Reuben, Gad, Manasseh
decisions.reason: Readable names the tribes instead of using the forms "Reubenites", "Gadites" and "Manassites".

source.text: וְזֹ֖את הַתּוֹרָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֣ם מֹשֶׁ֔ה לִפְנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And this [is] the law that set Moses before [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: And this [is] the law that Moses set before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.
en.B: This is the law that Moses laid before the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.
en.R: These are the teachings Moses gave to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: this: a heading for what follows
decisions.reason: Verses 44-49 introduce Moses' second speech, which begins at 5:1 and holds the main body of the law (chapters 5-26).

decisions.choice: law: Moses' teaching
decisions.reason: As at 1:5, the word means instruction, the whole of what Moses teaches.

decisions.choice: teachings
decisions.reason: Readable says "teachings" for the law, as Deuteronomy's terms call for.

source.text: אֵ֚לֶּה הָֽעֵדֹ֔ת וְהַֽחֻקִּ֖ים וְהַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּצֵאתָ֖ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: These [are] the testimonies and the statutes and the judgments that spoke Moses to [the] sons of Israel when they came out from Egypt,

en.L: These [are] the testimonies and the statutes and the judgments that Moses spoke to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel when they came out of Egypt,
en.B: These are the decrees, statutes, and rulings that Moses spoke to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} after they came out of Egypt,
en.R: These are the solemn instructions, laws, and rules that Moses gave the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} after they came out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: testimonies: the solemn terms of the covenant
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning to witness or to declare solemnly. It names the covenant's terms as God's charge to his people (6:17, 20).

decisions.choice: when they came out: in the time after the exodus, on the journey
decisions.reason: Moses spoke these words in the fortieth year after leaving Egypt (1:3). "When they came out" covers the whole period of the journey.

decisions.choice: decrees / solemn instructions
decisions.reason: Balanced says "decrees" and Readable "solemn instructions", since "testimonies" now suggests evidence given in court. Literal keeps "testimonies".

source.text: בְּעֵ֨בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֜ן בַּגַּ֗יְא מ֚וּל בֵּ֣ית פְּע֔וֹר בְּאֶ֗רֶץ סִיחֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּחֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִכָּ֤ה מֹשֶׁה֙ וּבְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּצֵאתָ֖ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: across the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth-peor, in [the] land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, whom struck Moses and [the] sons of Israel when they came out from Egypt.

en.L: across the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, whom Moses and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel struck down when they came out of Egypt.
en.B: across the Jordan in the valley opposite Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon. Moses and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} defeated him after they came out of Egypt.
en.R: Moses spoke to them on the east side of the Jordan River, in the valley across from Beth-peor. This was in the land of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled from Heshbon. Moses and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} defeated him after they left Egypt.

decisions.choice: Sihon, whom Moses struck down: the victory of 2:24-37
