decisions.reason: Sihon king of Heshbon refused Israel passage and was defeated (2:24-37; Numbers 21:21-31).

decisions.choice: dwelt: lived as king, reigned
decisions.reason: The verb means to sit or dwell. Of a king it means to sit on the throne, to reign (1:4).

decisions.choice: the valley opposite Beth-peor: Israel's camp in Moab
decisions.reason: Beth-peor ("house of Peor") was near the Peor of verse 3. Israel camped in the valley across from it (3:29), and Moses was buried there (34:6).

decisions.choice: Moses spoke to them on the east side of the Jordan River
decisions.reason: Readable, which ended verse 45 with a full stop, repeats that Moses spoke and says plainly that the place was east of the Jordan.

source.text: וַיִּֽירְשׁ֨וּ אֶת־אַרְצ֜וֹ וְאֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ׀ע֣וֹג מֶֽלֶךְ־הַבָּשָׁ֗ן שְׁנֵי֙ מַלְכֵ֣י הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן מִזְרַ֖ח שָֽׁמֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they took possession of his land and [the] land of Og king of Bashan, two kings of the Amorites who [were] across the Jordan toward [the] rising of [the] sun,

en.L: And they took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites who [were] across the Jordan toward the rising of the sun,
en.B: They took possession of his land and of the land of Og king of Bashan, those two kings of the Amorites who ruled across the Jordan, toward the sunrise,
en.R: They took possession of Sihon's land and also the land of Og, king of Bashan. These were the two Amorite kings who ruled on the east side of the Jordan River.

decisions.choice: Og king of Bashan: the second victory, 3:1-11
decisions.reason: Og came out against Israel at Edrei and was defeated (3:1-11; Numbers 21:33-35). Sihon and Og are often named together (31:4; Psalm 135:11).

decisions.choice: his land: Sihon's land
decisions.reason: "His" points back to Sihon in verse 46.

decisions.choice: Sihon's land
decisions.reason: Readable names Sihon, since its verse 46 ended with another name.

source.text: מֵעֲרֹעֵ֞ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר עַל־שְׂפַת־נַ֧חַל אַרְנֹ֛ן וְעַד־הַ֥ר שִׂיאֹ֖ן ה֥וּא חֶרְמֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: from Aroer which [is] on [the] edge of [the] wadi Arnon and to Mount Siyon, that [is] Hermon,

en.L: from Aroer, which [is] on the edge of the wadi Arnon, and as far as Mount Siyon, that [is] Hermon,
en.B: from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley as far as Mount Siyon, that is, Hermon,
en.R: Their land went from the town of Aroer, at the edge of the Arnon River valley, all the way north to Mount Siyon, which is Mount Hermon.

decisions.choice: Siyon: another name for Hermon
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "Siyon". This name for Hermon is found only here. The ancient Syriac version has "Sirion", the name 3:9 gives as the Sidonians' name for Hermon, and some think Siyon is a miscopying of it. The text as it stands is followed here.

decisions.choice: from Aroer on the Arnon to Hermon: the whole land east of the Jordan, south to north
decisions.reason: The Arnon gorge was the southern border of Sihon's land (2:36; 3:8, 12), and Mount Hermon the northern limit of Og's (3:8).

decisions.choice: wadi: a valley with a stream that runs in the rainy season
decisions.reason: The word names a valley or gorge and the stream in it. The Arnon cuts a deep gorge into the plateau east of the Dead Sea.

decisions.choice: Their land went ... all the way north
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and adds "north" so readers can follow the boundary.

source.text: וְכָל־הָ֨עֲרָבָ֜ה עֵ֤בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ מִזְרָ֔חָה וְעַ֖ד יָ֣ם הָעֲרָבָ֑ה תַּ֖חַת אַשְׁדֹּ֥ת הַפִּסְגָּֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: and all the Arabah across the Jordan eastward, and to [the] sea of the Arabah, under the slopes of the Pisgah.

en.L: and all the Arabah across the Jordan eastward, and as far as the sea of the Arabah, under the slopes of Pisgah.
en.B: and all the Arabah across the Jordan to the east, as far as the Sea of the Arabah, below the slopes of Pisgah.
en.R: It also included all the Jordan Valley on the east side of the river, as far south as the Dead Sea, below the slopes of Mount Pisgah.

decisions.choice: the Arabah: the deep rift valley of the Jordan and the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: The word means dry or desert land. It names the low valley through which the Jordan runs south into the Dead Sea (1:1; 3:17).

decisions.choice: the sea of the Arabah: the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: It is also called the Salt Sea (3:17; Joshua 3:16).

decisions.choice: slopes: the hillsides running down from Pisgah
decisions.reason: The word is rare and may mean slopes or the springs at their foot. It is the same phrase as in 3:17.

decisions.choice: the Jordan Valley ... the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Readable uses the names a modern reader knows, as at 3:17.
